title: [3.x] Add `wake_neighbours` option for `CollisionObject`
body: A longstanding series of physics bugs in 3.x is that moving physics objects via `set_transform()` does not wake other physics objects that are hit during the move (such as `RigidBodies`). This PR adds an optional feature to automatically wake objects that are paired with the moved body. ## Explanation I wasn't altogether clear whether the inability to wake up objects (unless using methods like `move_and_slide`) was a feature (performance optimization) or a bug. Anyway I added this feature while working on `NavPhysics` and realised it would be worthwhile it it's own right to be available for existing physics objects. I added the backend for `Kinematic`, but turns out it works for `Static` too: * `GodotPhysics` `Static` wake up neighbours fine already (there is no bug) * `Bullet` `Static` do not wake up neighbours normally, but they use the same path as `Kinematic` so this fix works for them too ## API I'm in two minds whether we should just enable this in all cases, using the existing `body_set_state` with a transform, or use e.g. the extra parameter in the new `body_set_transform()` function I've introduced here. Making it optional seems somewhat safer, in case the new mode causes changes in: * performance * behaviour I've also defaulted to off for backward compatibility. If there are no problems regarding changes in behaviour, we could possibly move to this as a default in the future and deprecate the `wake_neighbours` flag. ## Test Project [WakeNeighbours.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33025422/WakeNeighbours.zip) Use the cursors to move the box into the rigid body box. Wait 10 seconds then move. Before the PR, the boxes will interpenetrate as the rigid body has gone to sleep. After the PR the boxes will interact no matter how long they are apart. ## Previous workarounds Before this PR, if you wanted to move e.g. `Kinematic` without `MoveAndSlide`, you had to resort to hacks: * Turning off the ability to sleep for `RigidBodies` (hugely expensive unless you have few objects) * Setting up an `Area` and a `CollisionShape` _around_ your `Kinematic` for the specific purpose of waking up bodies, perform collision detect with this area, iterate manually through the collisions and activate each `RigidBody`. In short it was a mess. Now it can be done with one toggle on the object, and no extra nodes / performance required. ## Notes * Works for `GodotPhysics` and `Bullet`. * Performance in both cases should be good, as the pairing lists are already calculated, so I'm hoping the only cost is the activated objects (which you would want to activate anyway). * Adds a wrapper version of `body_set_transform()` in the `PhysicsServer` base class so that third party physics engines will still compile and run fine (but they won't offer this new ability unless they add relevant code).
